claim: The Federal Banking Agency Audit Act of 1978 (Pub. L. 95-320) created broad GAO authority to audit the Board and Reserve Banks for the first time, while deliberately excluding core monetary-policy areas. Before 1978 GAO had no general audit authority, though it held narrower authority over Treasury fiscal-agent work and currency-destruction review.
falsification: GAO records showing broader pre-1978 authority

notes.ceiling: THE PRE-1978 POSITION MUST NOT BE OVERSTATED AS LITERALLY ZERO CONTACT. F01 explicitly corrects that overstatement and the correction travels with the claim.
notes.verification_status: TRANSPOSED from F01 - not independently re-verified against the underlying record in this session
